report_notes.new: $\chi(r)=1$ for $r\le1$ and $\chi(r)=0$ for $r\ge2$; hence $m_R(x)=1$ for $|x|\le R$ and $m_R(x)=0$ for $|x|\ge2R$.

report_notes.disposition: The public Evidence jumps from Step1 to Step3. It gives no equivalent-norm/core/completion derivation of the assigned unmasked H1 form domain, despite the final AUDIT/limits assertions. Reported COMPLETE reading flags and PASS/high remain literal; full requested public reconstruction is not obtained for this step. The existing source supplies the argument; this author-side confirmation does not repair or expand the report.

mathematical_checks: The tempered-measure cutoff yields polynomial ball mass; annular weights sum because L>N. For the physical normalized p_epsilon and its derivatives, rapid decay gives all needed local x Fubini/differentiation majorants. The spectral multiplier is exp(-epsilon|xi|^2/2) with no extra normalization. Continuous distribution equality plus modulus-one phase and physical positivity gives 0<=Gamma*p_epsilon(x)<=Gamma*p_epsilon(0); a nonzero positive measure and strictly positive Gaussian give a strict value at zero. The report substantively reconstructs the added annular and phase arguments.

The compactly supported zero extension of Psi is smooth. A fixed Gaussian dominates each test derivative on its common compact spatial support; convolution positivity and the heat envelope then bound all spatial x uniformly. With r=s-t and s in compact I, r stays in a common compact interval, where |r|^-a is integrable for a<1. Derivatives fall on Psi rather than the singular power, so dominated differentiation and the first time derivative yield the stated supremum-norm Lipschitz estimate. The report uses these same operations and makes no directional-decay assertion.

The report correctly reconstructs the two imaginary-parameter resolvent/adjoint argument: both Ran(H-ib) and Ran(H+ib) are all L2, and ker(H*-ib)=Ran(H+ib)^perp=0. The bounded spectral projection near finite E_s supplies H2 Rayleigh tests. Splitting f=u+iv retains both real components and their squared-norm weighted quotient; it does not pick Re(f) alone. The same fixed compact common trial makes E_s<=-epsilon0, while h<=M gives E_s>=-M, and the square-root denominator is at least 2sqrt(epsilon0). However, the public Evidence section skips assigned Step2 entirely: the source derives D((H+1+M)^(1/2))=H1 by equivalence of half-power/H1 norms on H2 and both core/completion arguments. That reconstruction is not present in the report; its closing claims that the form-domain machinery is checked or upstream do not supply it. Author-side checking finds that source step coherent and unchanged, but cannot substitute for the missing public reviewer derivation.

F and chi give nested smooth radial m_R, and the common compact trial fixes R0 before comparison. For each real unit H1 test, 0<=m_R h_s f^2<=M f^2 and pointwise convergence identify its unmasked integral. Supremum over (R,f) is a numerical product-index supremum; positive square roots give increasing rates. Continuous nonnegative rate differences and nested open sets on compact I give uniform convergence, then numerical supremum of fixed-mask original-point lower bounds gives 2 I_Psi-v_Psi/2. There is no simultaneous R(T), random unmasked flow or uniform-in-R noise estimate. The original control/noise covariance and variance cost stay fixed; m_R h_s itself changes with the physical mask. The report final sentence is valid in this original-control context and is not a covariance assertion about a masked noise field.

The report preserves the different changes of variables: Radon pushforward gives r^(alpha-d), control amplitude r^(d+2-alpha), and mean r^2; cost has the further mean factor r^2 and Lebesgue Jacobian r^-d, hence r^(4-alpha). The real H1 Rayleigh tests U_r are a bijection with kinetic and potential energies both r^2, so lambda scales r and I scales r. D_(1/r) is the inverse on the full nonnegative nonzero smooth class. The H2 operator identity is supplementary and consistent. Time and a fixed mask radius are not invariantly rescaled.

With k=3-alpha>0, q=k+1, r0^k=I0/v0, the coefficient-one value equals r0 I0/2>0. With rc=c^(1/k), both c rc and rc^q equal Kc=c^(q/k); a bijection scales the entire score set. The independent canonical point upper bound has a logarithmically negligible prefactor; together with the already assigned lower bound it gives a finite real Q2 and a uniform ceiling on all coefficient-two scores. Scaling at c=2 then bounds the coefficient-one set before finite-real suprema are taken. Positivity, full set equality and Kc>0 yield S_c=Kc S_1 and Q2>=S_2. No optimizer, first-mean/source identification, unconditional numerical Jensen improvement or extension of strict positivity to Gamma=0 is inferred.
